claims.statement: The EU WEEE framework prioritizes preventing waste and promotes reuse, recycling, recovery, and recovery of secondary raw materials from electrical and electronic equipment.

contrary_evidence: Reuse goals do not waive WEEE, producer-responsibility, battery, transport, or product-safety obligations.
Some removed units may have no safe resale path and must go directly to authorized treatment.

economics.acquisition_route: Installer agreements, insurer repair channels, distributors, and equipment-owner service contracts
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is a partner-operated national network handling thousands of units annually, with transaction margin and a proprietary reliability dataset
economics.founder_time: Initially 12-20 hours per week with pickup, storage, and hazardous handling outsourced
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 40-65% after contracted logistics, testing, buyer returns, and recycler fees, without speculative inventory purchases
economics.payback: Unknown until residual-value distribution and lawful handling cost are sampled
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 300-1500 PLN triage or pickup fee plus 15-25% of recovered resale value
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installers generate repeat removals; buyer repeat depends on consistent grading and volume

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive supply density, serialized test histories, buyer demand data, and efficient reverse-logistics routes improve unit economics
fingerprint.customer: Refurbishers, spare-parts buyers, secondary equipment users, and installers seeking compliant removal routes
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Start with the family installer and recruit regional installers, insurance repair networks, and specialist refurbishers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Pre-agreed pickup rights, serial-level intake, outsourced testing, consignment resale, parts harvesting, and authorized-recycler routing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installers or owners pay a triage/removal fee, and buyers pay on tested equipment or parts transfer; the company retains a commission
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A repair, upgrade, insurance event, or repowering job creates removed equipment with uncertain residual value and disposal obligations

founder_fit: Immediate sourcing access through renewable installers
Data-based grading and routing use analytical skills
Can start asset-light with consignment and licensed partners
Creates a scalable supply and data network
risks: Waste, battery, transport, and storage rules may require permits
Resold electrical equipment creates safety and warranty liability
Stolen or encumbered equipment could enter the network
Low residual value may not cover reverse logistics

structure.control_point: First-refusal and title-transfer rights over deinstalled equipment at the moment of replacement
structure.critical_dependency: Equipment must be lawfully classified, safely transported, economically testable, and valuable to repeat buyers

thesis: Contract with installers, insurers, and asset owners for first refusal on removed inverters, panels, heat pumps, batteries, and chargers, then test and route reusable units to refurbishers while sending true waste to authorized recyclers.
title: Renewable Equipment First-Refusal Recovery Network
uncertainties: Unknown annual removal volume per installer
Unknown share that remains a reusable product rather than regulated waste
No refurbisher pricing or return rate is validated
Polish waste-law classification needs specialist review
